=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Hand-back step 1 deletes the safety-net trigger by id with `(delete_trigger, ignore not-found), its own implement-plan <slug>: safety net bound to this session` and then adds the cleanup-call annotation — but does NOT call get_trigger first to verify ownership. CLAUDE.md §26.I (lines 2165+) prescribes `get_trigger` ownership verification for triggers named by id, and §26.I explicitly enumerates "a checker's own hand-back trigger" and "an arming report" as id-source examples that require the check (the safety-net id here comes from the arming report, recorded by `Record the ids (Checker:, Safety-net:, Hand-back:)` at the end of arming-the-wait).
  WHY: When an unattended stage session executes the hand-back procedure, it deletes the safety-net trigger by its recorded id. The safety-net id comes from the arming report, which §26.I lists as an id-source requiring get_trigger verification. While the safety-net was created by this session in arming-the-wait step 4 and bound to this session, that is by construction not by verification; an unguarded delete trusts the id from an arming report / progress log verbatim, exactly the pattern that produced the #5068 incident (`trig_012QFMb1nQkFFs1JyPsnZVsE` no longer existed; the session was blocked retrying it). `ignore not-found` handles only the already-deleted case — only get_trigger distinguishes that from `id-repurposed-by-another-Routine`.
- CLAUDE.md | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: §26.D's terminal path describes deleting the fired Routine by id with `delete_trigger, ignoring not-found` and adds the cleanup-call annotation, but does NOT add the get_trigger ownership verification §26.I prescribes.
  WHY: When an unattended fixer session executes the terminal path, it deletes the fired hand-back Routine by id. While that Routine was created by this session in arming-the-wait and is inherently owned by construction, that is by construction not by verification; a repurposed id would target a foreign Routine.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Delete only what is yours, and say so first. Before a `delete_trigger` on a trigger named by id (a `— resume.` block, the progress log, an arming report, a checker's own hand-back trigger), read it with `get_trigger`. Not found → already done; skip the delete. Delete it only when its `name` is one the flow creates for this project or pull request (`implement-plan <slug>: …`, `PR #<n> …`) and its `persistent_session_id` is a session of that project or pull request (the previous stage session, the checker, or this session)" (CLAUDE.md §26.I, lines 2165+). Plan step 2 (docs/plans/issue-5068-skip-denied-cleanup-calls-plan.md:66) explicitly lists "Hand-back steps 1–2" alongside "step 0 resume hygiene (with the `get_trigger` ownership check)" as sites where §26.I applies with the ownership check. PR DESCRIPTION "Changes and evidence" row also lists `implement-plan-claude.md` twin: ... hand-back (`249`).
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md hand-back step 1 (around line 278); and the corresponding contract assertion in tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py::test_other_cleanup_sites_skip_a_denied_cleanup_call hand-back section assertion (around line 381).
  Evidence of absence: The diff replaces line 278 with a single-sentence cleanup annotation: `Deletes its pending safety net (delete_trigger, ignore not-found), its own implement-plan <slug>: safety net bound to this session. This delete and the rename in step 2 are cleanup calls (CLAUDE.md §26.I): a denied one is skipped and noted, never retried, and the intervention goes ahead.` This asserts ownership in prose only. By contrast, resume hygiene (line 11) is rewritten to include `each only after get_trigger shows it is this project's own: its name starts with implement-plan <slug>: and its persistent_session_id is the previous stage session or the checker. Not found means it is already gone, so skip the delete. Say what the check found in the text before the call.` The corresponding test at line 381 of test_implement_plan_claude_command.py asserts only `This delete and the rename in step 2 are cleanup calls (CLAUDE.md §26.I)` — the cleanup annotation only. It does NOT assert any `get_trigger` reference, unlike line 358 (`each only after get_trigger shows it is this project's own`) for resume hygiene.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: §26.I `Delete only what is yours, and say so first` rule applied to the §26.D terminal-path delete of the fired Routine (CLAUDE.md §26.I, lines 2165+). Plan step 2 does not list §26.D terminal explicitly, but §26.I's wording covers `a checker's own hand-back trigger` and the PR DESCRIPTION points to `CLAUDE.md:1948`, `1981` as the updated sites.
  Expected change site: CLAUDE.md §26.D terminal bullet (around lines 1981-2002); the corresponding contract assertion in tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py::test_claude_md_26_flows_point_to_26i (around lines 332-336).
  Evidence of absence: §26.D terminal bullet (line 1984 in the new file) reads `and only then deletes the fired Routine (delete_trigger, ignoring not-found)` followed by the cleanup-call annotation at lines 1999-2002, but does NOT add a `get_trigger` ownership check before the delete. The corresponding test in tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py at lines 332-336 asserts only `The rename, the archive, and the delete are cleanup calls (§26.I)` and `a denied archive therefore skips the delete, which keeps the order safe` and `The sweep's deletes and the rename are cleanup calls (§26.I)` — the cleanup annotation — but does NOT assert any `get_trigger` reference.
